display.purpose: Hero headline only. Appears once per page. font-weight 900, tight tracking.

shadows.name: card-lift

shadows.name: dialog-lift

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Full Ink fill at rest. Inverts to white on hover. Physical scale press.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; background: oklch(0.145 0 0); color: oklch(1 0 0); border: 1px solid oklch(0.145 0 0); padding: 10px 20px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0.18em; text-transform: uppercase; border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1); transform-origin: center; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(1 0 0); color: oklch(0.145 0 0); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); transition: transform 150ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px oklch(0.145 0 0), 0 0 0 4px oklch(1 0 0); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Transparent. Border-faint at rest, sharpens to ink on hover. Used for secondary and tertiary actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; background: transparent; color: oklch(0.708 0 0); border: 1px solid oklch(0.708 0 0 / 40%); padding: 6px 12px; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0.15em; text-transform: uppercase; border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer; transition: color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1), border-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: oklch(0.145 0 0); border-color: oklch(0.145 0 0); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: oklch(0.145 0 0); }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Dispute actions only. Transparent background, destructive border and text. Hover tints background faintly.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; background: transparent; color: oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325); border: 1px solid oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325 / 50%); padding: 6px 12px; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0.15em; text-transform: uppercase; border-radius: 0; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1); } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background: oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325 / 8%); }

narrative.overview:
Covert's visual language is borrowed from classified document design: dense information without decoration, high contrast without flourish, hierarchy expressed entirely through weight and tracking. Every element earns its place. Nothing introduces itself; everything presents itself.

The system rejects crypto's standard aesthetic reflex — neon on black, gradient text, glassmorphism as atmosphere — and refuses the inverse reflex too: it is not trying to look like a friendly SaaS tool. It occupies a third position: precision document. Think redacted government file, not dashboard. The monochrome is not a limitation; it is the argument.

Color plays zero decorative role. The single chromatic exception is the destructive (dispute/error) state. Its rarity is structural. Everything else is achromatic.
keyCharacteristics: Zero-radius borders on every interactive element (sharp = precise)
All-caps labels with wide tracking (0.18–0.22em) as the primary labeling language
Ink-on-white as the default surface; black-on-black for the private/shielded context
Offset shadow (4px 4px 0 0 #000) on hover for service cards — tactile without softness
scale(0.97) press feedback on all primary buttons — physical confirmation of intent

rules.name: The One Chromatic Rule
rules.body: Color exists only to signal a state requiring immediate attention (dispute, error) or a system boundary (private/shielded context). It never appears for decoration, branding, or visual interest. If you are adding color to make something look better, stop.

rules.name: The Label Law
rules.body: Every UI label — section headers, table columns, button text, status chips, eyebrows, nav links — is ALL CAPS with tracking ≥0.18em. No exceptions.

rules.name: The Weight-Only Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy is carried by weight contrast (400 vs 900), not by large size differences alone.

rules.name: The Zero-Blur Rule
rules.body: No soft ambient shadows, no blur in any shadow value. If depth is expressed, it is expressed through hard-edge offset shadows only.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces rest flat. The card lift shadow appears only on hover. The dialog shadow appears only in modal context. Nothing is elevated at rest.

dos: Do use zero border-radius on every interactive element: buttons, inputs, cards, chips, dialogs.
Do write every UI label in ALL CAPS with letter-spacing: 0.18em minimum.
Do express button hover as a full fill-inversion (ink to white or white to ink).
Do use the hard-edge 4px 4px 0 0 offset shadow exclusively for card hover lift.
Do use the Private Surface black only for the shielded/TEE balance context.
Do use scale(0.97) on :active for all primary buttons.
Do use cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) for entry animations (0.75s) and cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) for micro-interactions (150ms).
donts: Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text). Forbidden.
Don't use neon, vivid color washes, or glow effects.
Don't use glassmorphism decoratively. The navbar backdrop-blur is the only functional instance.
Don't add soft ambient shadows. The Zero-Blur Rule is absolute.
Don't use rounded corners. Every corner is 0px.
Don't animate layout properties. Animate transform and opacity only.
Don't use ease-in or linear timing.
Don't use transition: all. Always declare specific properties.
